name: ex-USSR Kinship Research
works_with: Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes
short: A genealogy skill that turns your agent into a careful family history researcher for the former USSR and Russian Empire.
what: The skill covers all 15 former Soviet republics. Your agent reads church books, civil records, military, deportation and repression files and unindexed archive scans, and keeps every find traceable. Claims get plain statuses such as `single-source` or `corroborated`, and an audit script flags weak corroboration before you write conclusions. The instructions are in Russian, but the agent talks to you in your own language, and the default result is an HTML report with a family tree.
who: Anyone researching family roots in the former Soviet Union who wants evidence they can check. It refuses to look up current addresses, phones or accounts of living people, so it is no use for finding someone today.
needs: Python 3 (most scripts need only the standard library)
Node.js, only for the optional Skills CLI
Pillow for `scan_montage.py`, and Chrome, Chromium or Edge for PDF export, both optional

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: The CLI lets you pick your agent and installs into the current project by default. Add `-g` to install it for every project.

steps.title: Or clone it into your agent's skills folder
steps.text: For Codex, clone into `~/.codex/skills/` instead. For one project, put the folder in `.claude/skills/` inside the repo.

steps.title: Start a case outside the skill folder
steps.text: Run this from the skill folder. Keep private case data outside the skill's Git checkout.

steps.title: Check the evidence before the report

try.label: From the README
try.text: My great-grandfather was exiled to Kazakhstan in the 1930s. Help me find his parents in church records.

watch: When you authorise it, the agent can send requests to archives, libraries and museums by email or official web tools. The README says connecting a mailbox alone does not authorise sending, attachments or paid services.
It uses your own signed in browser session for FamilySearch, and you do the sign ins yourself. It may try a CAPTCHA once and then hands it to you.
It does not upload your documents or DNA data to third party services without your explicit consent.
Case files hold personal family data, so keep them out of the skill's checkout and check staged files before you contribute.
